text:
tara: Quick RFC follow-up — proposal to make regional TLS boundaries explicit for Private deployments. idea: control plane stays global (management API only), but each region has its own regional-relay cert chain and DNS redirect so traffic never leaves the nearest relay in plaintext.

sachin: tl;dr on why we need that vs end-to-end mTLS from customer -> controlplane?

tara: two reasons: 1) latency + egress cost — if relay is regional we avoid cross-region hairpin and can preserve source IP for billing. 2) cert lifecycle & trust model: issuing short-lived region certs via customer-trusted CA reduces our need for long-lived cross-account certs.

evan: are we talking TLS termination at the regional-relay (TLS offload) or TLS passthrough + mTLS to CP?

tara: regional-relay terminates TLS for dataplane, then mTLS to control plane for control messages only. dataplane connections to model-serving pods use a local trust boundary (region cert).

maria: security concern: who signs the region certs? if we manage CA, customers may push back for private deployments. need HSM/KMS integration.

tara: agree — option A: customer uploads a CA cert + we mint region certs (recommended for regulated customers). option B: Redwood-managed regional CA with audit logs for standard customers. both supported in config.

sachin: operationally, how do we rotate without downtime? want seamless rotation and fallback to previous certs for 5m.

tara: rollout plan in my head: v1 allow dual-cert (old+new) on relays, issue new certs in parallel, then switch DNS SRV targets to new relays. provide canary % by region. fallback: SRV swap back.

evan: SRV records? are we using SRV or ALIAS CNAME trick? link to DNS failure modes? SRV isn't universally supported by all clients.

tara: good catch — for our SDKs we can use SRV internally, but for customers that rely on native LB behavior we'll provide Route53 ALIAS + health checks option. internal controlplane->relay uses SRV. external endpoints: ALIAS.

maria: need to document expected TLS headers and SANs so customer's WAFs allow it. SAN will include region-relay.<customer-domain> and relay-node ids.

sachin: what about source-IP preservation? NAT currently rewrites to shared egress. if we put relays in customer subnets (private endpoint mode) we can preserve source IP, but that implies sidecar or relay agent inside VPC.

tara: exactly — two modes: "relay-in-vpc" (preserve src ip, customer-managed route; recommended for Dedicated/Private) and "regional-managed-relay" (Redwood-managed subnets, no src ip preservation). toggleable by customer.

evan: rollout ops checklist please: how do oncall debug cert chain issues cross-account? we need a tooling page that given trace_id outputs relay cert state, CA fingerprint, and last rotate time.

tara: will add to runbook. infra-bot: create ticket template for cert-rotation postmortem and a script to fetch relay certs (node -> cert chain -> fingerprint).

infra-bot: created ticket #NET-1384 and added a skeleton script at infra/tools/relay-cert-inspector. :white_check_mark:

maria: one more constraint: telemetry. we must ensure trace spans include region-relay hop (obf host) and a flag whether source-ip preserved. this helps billing and SLO analysis.

tara: agreed. final ask: thumbs up if this pattern is acceptable: global controlplane (management only) + region-relay TLS boundary + dual CA modes + relay-in-vpc opt-in for src-ip preservation. :thumbsup:

sachin: +1 from infra side.

evan: +1 for SDKs/docs work. I'll take SRV/ALIAS compatibility PR.

maria: +1 but need compliance signoff for managed CA option. I'll loop security.

tara: thanks all — I'll draft a short RFC + rollout playbook and link the tools. follow-up: I'll post the RFC link here when ready.
